newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - HK lengthens yield curve.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - HK lengthens yield curve.

text.p: Asian debt markets were quiet on Monday, with Hong Kong's launch of its debut 10-year government bond issue the main attraction.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) sold HK$500 million in 7.37 percent bonds due 2006 at an average accepted yield of 7.57 percent.

"With this tender, the Hong Kong government capital market is a fully mature market comparable to the Australian, French or German markets," said Andrew Fung, head of capital markets, Asia, at Commonwealth Bank of Australia in Hong Kong.
"In most of the mature markets, the liquid yield curve is only extended to 10 years. Only the U.S. market is exceptional with the 30-year liquid benchmark," he added.
Up to now, the longest tenor issue offered by the HKMA has been seven years.
The issue was a 13.5 times oversubscribed with HK$7.26 billion applied, a record oversubscription for a Hong Kong note tender.
Traders said the huge demand suggested that the 10-year issue attracted institutional investors as well as market makers in Exchange Fund Notes (EFN).
The issue rallied almost immediately after launch to yield 7.55 percent, traders said.
The notes priced to yield 93 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. Prior to the tender, the notes were trading at a spread of 96-97 basis points in the grey market, traders said.
They said further tightening is possible.

The 10-year notes will be offered on a quarterly basis. Some traders have charged that tendering new notes four times a year could flood the market with unwanted paper, steepening the yield curve at the long end.
But others said such worries were misplaced.

"This morning's results show that there is a substantial demand for 10-year paper by some private investors, so the market is not totally in the hands of market makers," said an EFN trader at a U.S. bank here.

In other news, bankers said pre-marketing has begun on Union Bank of the Philippines' US$75 million floating rate certificates of deposit issue, which will be formally launched into general syndication on November 4.
The certificates carry a maturity of five years with put and a call options in year three. They will pay a coupon of 85 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 93 basis points. Merrill Lynch, Standard Chartered Investment Banking, LTCB Asia and Dresdner South East Asia are arrangers.
Chekiang First Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, has mandated three banks to arrange a HK$500 million FRCD issue.

The certificates will carry a maturity of five years with put and call options in years three and four. The all-in return is reported to be around 65 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Schroders Asia is the bookrunner. The other arrangers are DKB Asia and Commerz (East Asia). General syndication is expected this week.
